stories.title: Canada's Prime Minister Carney Supports EU Associate Membership Proposal
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has expressed strong support for the European Union's proposal for Canada to become its first 'associate member'. In a speech to the European Parliament, Carney emphasized the potential for a closer alliance, stating that it would create a 'beacon for other democracies' and enhance Canada's sovereignty against external pressures. He highlighted shared values and the importance of cooperation between Canada and the EU in a changing geopolitical landscape.

stories.title: Ireland to Boycott Eurovision Again Over Israel's Participation Amid Gaza Conflict
stories.summary: Ireland's national broadcaster has announced a boycott of the 2027 Eurovision Song Contest for the second consecutive year. The decision is in protest against Israel's participation, citing the ongoing loss of lives in Gaza as a significant factor. Ireland joins other countries, including the Netherlands, Iceland, Slovenia, and Spain, in this protest.

stories.title: U.N. Experts Find Grounds to Believe U.S. Committed War Crimes in Iran Strikes
stories.summary: A United Nations fact-finding mission has concluded there are reasonable grounds to believe that the United States committed war crimes during two military strikes in Iran in February. These strikes targeted a school and a sports facility, resulting in significant civilian casualties, including the deaths of 156 civilians, among them 120 children. The findings suggest that these actions may constitute violations of international law.

stories.title: Sweden's Prime Minister Resigns Following Centre-Left Election Victory
stories.summary: Ulf Kristersson, Sweden's Prime Minister from the centre-right, has announced his resignation after the centre-left bloc, led by Magdalena Andersson, won a narrow majority in the recent parliamentary elections. The left-wing opposition secured 176 seats compared to the ruling bloc's 173, prompting Kristersson's decision to step down and allowing Andersson to attempt to form a new government. Coalition negotiations are expected to be challenging as parliament prepares for the government formation process.

stories.title: US Denies Visa to Palestinian Officials Ahead of UN General Assembly
stories.summary: The US State Department has extended visa sanctions on Palestinian officials, including President Mahmoud Abbas, preventing them from attending the upcoming UN General Assembly in New York. This marks the second consecutive year that the US has barred Abbas and other officials from entering the country for the event, which the Palestinian Authority has condemned.

stories.title: Analysis Links Climate Change to Deadly Glacier and Rock Collapse in Nepal
stories.summary: Scientists have concluded that climate change significantly contributed to a recent glacier and rock collapse in Nepal, which resulted in nearly 1,400 deaths and left thousands missing. The warming climate has destabilized glaciers and thawed ground, creating conditions that led to the disaster. The combined toll from the incident now stands at 1,446 dead and at least 6,669 missing.

stories.title: Macklemore Donates $1 Million to Palestinian Aid Amid Tour Controversy
stories.summary: Macklemore has pledged $1 million to Palestinian humanitarian aid organizations and has challenged Robert Kraft to match his donation. This announcement follows Macklemore's removal from Ed Sheeran's US tour after he made pro-Palestinian comments on stage. The stadium owner revealed that Sheeran had previously requested Kraft to match a $2 million donation for aid in the region.

stories.title: Escalation in Yemen Conflict Leaves Five Fatalities Amid Houthi and Saudi Attacks
stories.summary: Recent clashes between the Houthis, the Yemeni government, and Saudi Arabia have resulted in at least five fatalities. Saudi Arabia reported that one fatality was caused by drone shrapnel, while the Houthis denied any attack on Mecca.
